ingest.description:
Parse log files into a stored log set (one per cluster node) and print its manifest.

PATHs are files, directories or ZIP files (directories are scanned
non-recursively for *.log*; rotated files x.log.N (also gzipped, x.log.N.gz,
identified by its decompressed content) are read oldest first; a
ZIP is extracted into the data directory, job.json and *.log* files only, at most
32 GiB, and removed afterwards). Files found in a directory that the format
does not recognise in their first 200 lines (access, GC or JSON logs next
to atlassian-jira.log) are skipped and listed in "ingest.skipped", and so
are side logs next to their main log (atlassian-jira-security.log,
-outgoing-mail.log, -slow-queries.log beside atlassian-jira.log); files
named explicitly are read, except one over 64 MiB that the format does not
recognise at all (error "not_in_format"; --force reads it). Lines over 1 MiB
are cut, and an entry keeps at most 4 Mi characters and 100,000 lines
("parse_error": "entry truncated: N lines, M bytes"). The log-set id is
derived from the file digests, so ingesting the same files again is a no-op
that prints the existing manifest (use --overwrite to rebuild it). Progress
goes to stderr.

Cluster logs become one set per node (--split auto): a cluster log export
(a ZIP or folder with job.json and NODE_atlassian-jira.log* files), files
named NODE_atlassian-jira.log* of two or more nodes, or one directory whose
sub-directories (two or more) hold one node's logs each. --split prefix|dir
forces a kind, --split none keeps one set. Each node's set is named
PREFIX_node (PREFIX: --name, else --cluster, else the first 8 characters of
the capture id) and labelled with its node, the cluster (--cluster, else
that of the node's newest earlier set) and the capture id (--capture, else
the export's jobId, else a hash of the set ids). A single set gets --node,
--cluster (default: the node's earlier cluster) and --capture; when its log
names its node, a warning suggests --node.

Output (json): one set: the manifest, schema "logset.v1":
  {"schema": "logset.v1", "id", "name", "format",
   "sources": [{"path", "size", "xxh3", "first_ts", "last_ts", "entries"}],
   "first_ts", "last_ts", "entry_count", "group_count", "created_at",
   "tool_version", "schema_version", "signature_version",
   "mask_rules_version", "signature_spec", "recipe_key",
   "node", "cluster", "capture",
   "ingest": {"parsed_entries", "parse_errors", "elapsed_s", "existing",
              "skipped": [path, ...], "warnings": [str, ...]},
   "merges": [{"cluster_id", "signatures": [str], "drain_template"}]}
A split: {"schema": "ingest-capture.v1",
  "capture": {"capture", "cluster", "first_ts", "last_ts", "entry_count",
              "nodes": [{"node", "id", "name", "first_ts", "last_ts",
                         "entry_count"}]},
  "sets": [<logset.v1 with "ingest" as above>, ...], "warnings": [str]}
"merges" is present only with --mine; the proposals are also stored in
merges.parquet (the "merges" view of `query`).
"ingest.existing" is true when the set already existed and was reused (it
gets the node, cluster and capture it lacks); "ingest.warnings" then says
when --name was ignored (also on stderr).

Without --store and RAGNALOG_STORE the data directory is ./.ragnalog; inside a git
work tree it is not created (error "store_error": real logs could be
committed), but an existing ./.ragnalog is used.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 unknown --format, bad option, bad ZIP, a --split that
does not fit the input, or --node with a split; 2 no files found, format
not detected, a large named file not in the format, or no entries parsed
(manifest still printed); 3 store error (including a refused default data directory
inside a git work tree).

params.name: PATHS...
params.help: Log files, directories or ZIPs.

params.help: Format name (see `formats`); default: detected from the first 200 lines of the first file a format recognises (named files first).

params.name: --name
params.help: Human-readable alias for the set, usable wherever SET is expected; with a split, the prefix of the sets' names. No ':', '/' or backslash.

params.name: --frames
params.help: Add the top N stack frames to signatures (finer groups); default 0.

params.name: --overwrite
params.help: Rebuild the set if one with the same id already exists.

params.name: --mine
params.help: Propose group merges with Drain3 (needs extra "mine": uv sync --extra mine).

params.name: --force
params.help: Read a named file over 64 MiB even if none of its first 200 lines is in the format.

params.name: --node
params.help: Node (the cluster node id of the set, e.g. NODE1; only when the input is not split).

params.name: --cluster
params.help: Cluster (the name of the Jira instance of the nodes, e.g. jira-test; default: the cluster of the newest earlier set of the same node).

params.name: --capture
params.help: Capture (its id; default: the export's jobId, else a hash of the set ids when split, else none).

params.name: --split
params.help: Split (one set per node; auto: an export ZIP or folder with job.json, files named NODE_atlassian-jira.log* of two or more nodes, or one directory of node sub-directories; prefix and dir force a kind; none: one set).

sets.description:
List the log sets in the data directory, newest first.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "sets.v1", "store": str, "count": int,
   "items": [<logset.v1 manifest without "schema"> + "summary" + "stale"]}
Each item has id, name, format, sources, first_ts, last_ts, entry_count,
group_count, created_at, tool_version, schema_version, signature_version,
mask_rules_version, signature_spec, recipe_key, node, cluster, capture,
"summary": {"errors", "warnings", "error_groups"} (entries at ERROR/FATAL,
entries at WARN, groups at ERROR/FATAL; null when the set cannot be read)
and "stale": true when recipe_key differs from the recipe this version
signs the set's format and spec with (rebuild with `upgrade`; triage
does not use stale sets as baselines). node, cluster and capture say which
cluster node a set holds and which capture it belongs to (null when
unknown; see `label`, `captures`). --brief keeps only id, name, first_ts,
last_ts, entry_count, group_count, summary, stale, node and capture. An
empty or missing data directory gives count 0. A set directory whose manifest cannot be
read is not listed; one warning per such directory goes to stderr (clear it
by deleting its directory).

Exit codes: 0 ok (also when empty); 3 store error.

params.name: --brief
params.help: Only id, name, first_ts, last_ts, entry_count, group_count, summary, stale, node, capture.

set.description:
Print one log set: its manifest plus the severity summary of `sets`.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "logset.v1", <manifest keys, see `ingest`>,
   "summary": {"errors", "warnings", "error_groups"}}
"summary" counts the entries at ERROR/FATAL, the entries at WARN and the
groups at ERROR/FATAL, as in `sets` and GET /api/sets/{ref}. Table mode
prints the manifest as tables.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name.

captures.description:
List the captures (the sets of several nodes collected together).

A capture is the sets whose manifests share a "capture" id: one cluster log
export or one `ingest` that split its input into one set per node (also
`label --capture`). Newest last_ts first. Reads the manifests only.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "captures.v1", "count": int,
   "items": [{"capture", "cluster", "first_ts", "last_ts", "entry_count",
              "nodes": [{"node", "id", "name", "first_ts", "last_ts",
                         "entry_count"}]}]}
"nodes" are the member sets sorted by node; "cluster" is the members'
cluster. --brief keeps only node, id and name per node. A capture is
referred to as capture:ID (a unique prefix of its id), cluster:NAME (the
newest capture of the cluster) or cluster:NAME@YYYY-MM-DD.

Exit codes: 0 ok (also when empty); 3 store error.

params.name: --brief
params.help: Only node, id and name per node.

capture.description:
Show the nodes of a capture side by side: coverage, volume, top error, events, verdict.

REF is a capture (capture:ID, a unique id prefix; cluster:NAME, its newest
capture; cluster:NAME@YYYY-MM-DD) or a log set: the capture the set belongs
to, else that set as a capture of one node. Every capture view counts
within one window: --window overlap (default; the time all nodes have logs
for, so a group is not "only on NODE2" because NODE1's files start later),
union, or --since/--until. Each node is triaged against its own previous
set (never another node); --no-triage skips it.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "capture.v1", "capture": id | null, "cluster": str | null,
   "window": {"mode": "overlap" | "union" | "explicit", "since", "until"},
   "nodes": [{"node", "set": {"id", "name"}, "first_ts", "last_ts",
              "coverage": {"since", "until"} | null, "gaps": [[since, until]],
              "entries", "errors", "warnings", "errors_per_hour",
              "warnings_per_hour",
              "top_error": {"signature", "template", "count"} | null,
              "verdict": str | null, "baseline": {"id", "name", "reason"} | null,
              "events": {kind: count}}],
   "skew": [{"a", "b", "offset_ms", "pairs"}]}
"coverage" is the node's first to last entry within the window, "gaps"
runs of at least 15 minutes without entries inside it; rates are per hour
of coverage. "verdict" is the node's triage verdict (as `triage`;
no_baseline when it has no earlier set; null with --no-triage). "skew" is
a clock skew estimate from paired events, shown, never applied.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad option or time, or the nodes' logs do not
overlap (use --window union); 2 unknown capture; 3 unknown set or store
error.

params.name: REF
params.help: Capture (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@YYYY-MM-DD]) or log set.

params.name: --window
params.help: overlap or union (overlap: the latest first entry to the earliest last entry of the nodes, the time all of them have logs for; union: earliest to latest).

params.name: --since
params.help: From this time: ISO 8601 (naive = UTC), YYYY-MM-DD, or 30m/2h/1d before the capture's last entry (an explicit window instead of --window).

params.name: --until
params.help: Up to this time (same forms as --since; given alone, either one leaves the other end at the capture's first or last entry).

params.name: --triage
params.help: Verdict per node vs its own previous set (triage).

label.description:
Label a log set (its cluster node, cluster and capture).

Rewrites only the set's manifest: its id, name and data stay as they are.
An option that is not given keeps its value; an empty value (--node "")
clears it. Values are letters, digits, "_", "." and "-" (at most 128).
Sets that share a capture id are listed together by `captures`; triage
compares a set that has a node only with earlier sets of the same node.

Output (json): the manifest, {"schema": "logset.v1", ...} (see `ingest`).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 no option given or a bad value; 3 unknown set or store
error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name.

params.name: --node
params.help: Node (the cluster node id the logs come from, e.g. NODE1).

params.name: --cluster
params.help: Cluster (the name of the Jira instance of the node, e.g. jira-test).

params.name: --capture
params.help: Capture (its id: sets with the same capture are viewed together).

groups.usage: LOGSET [--level str] [--min-level str] [--logger str] [--since str] [--until str] [--with-exception] [--exception str] [--contains str] [--sort count|last_seen|first_seen|signature|template=count] [--limit int=50] [--offset int=0] [--coarse] [--columns str*] [--brief]
groups.description:
List the groups (one per message signature) of a log set.

A group collects all entries whose level, logger, masked message and
exception chain are equal; its "signature" (16 hex chars) is stable across
sets, so it can be used with `show`, `entries --signature` and `diff`.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "groups.v1", "logset": id, "count": int, "total": int,
   "offset": int, "next_offset": int | null, "truncated": bool, "items": [
    {"signature", "coarse_signature", "template", "level", "logger",
     "level_name", "exception_type", "count", "first_seen", "last_seen",
     ...}, ...]}
"level" is numeric (ERROR=50), "level_name" the name. "items" holds the
groups.v1 columns (`ragnalog schema groups`: also user_count, thread_count,
source_count, top_users, top_threads, sources, examples), at most --limit
rows starting at --offset (in --sort order). "total" is the number of
matching groups before --offset/--limit, "offset" echoes --offset and
"truncated" is true when more rows follow this page (offset + count <
total) and "next_offset" is where it starts (null on the last page). With --coarse, "signature"
is the coarse signature and "signatures" lists the member signatures.
--columns keeps only the named columns (comma-separated and/or repeated;
unknown name: error "invalid_value", "hint" lists the valid ones).
--brief is the preset --columns signature,template,level_name,logger,
exception_type,count,first_seen,last_seen; --brief with --columns is a
usage error.
--with-exception keeps groups that carry an exception (exception_type not
null) at any level, so a DEBUG entry with a stack trace is found even
though --min-level WARN would hide it. --exception TEXT matches a
case-insensitive substring of exception_type (the outermost exception);
--contains TEXT a case-insensitive substring of template. With --coarse
all filters apply to the member groups.

Exit codes: 0 ok (also when no group matches); 1 bad option, unknown
column, or --brief with --columns; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name.

params.name: --level
params.help: Only these levels, e.g. ERROR or WARN,ERROR (TRACE DEBUG INFO WARN ERROR FATAL; UNKNOWN = entries whose header could not be parsed).

params.name: --min-level
params.help: Only this level or more severe, e.g. WARN.

params.name: --logger
params.help: Logger name or package prefix (c.a.jira matches c.a.jira.Foo; com.atlassian.jira also the forms Jira abbreviates, c.a.jira.index.X and c.a.j.issue.index.X).

params.name: --since
params.help: Only groups with an entry at/after this time (last_seen >= since): ISO 8601 (naive = UTC), YYYY-MM-DD, or 30m/2h/1d before the set's last entry.

params.name: --until
params.help: Only groups first seen before this time (same forms as --since).

params.name: --with-exception
params.help: Only groups with an exception (exception_type not null), any level.

params.name: --exception
params.help: Only groups whose exception_type contains this text (case-insensitive).

params.name: --contains
params.help: Only groups whose template contains this text (case-insensitive).

params.name: --sort
params.help: count, last_seen (newest first), first_seen (oldest first), signature, template.

params.name: --limit
params.help: Maximum number of rows; 0 = all.

params.name: --offset
params.help: Skip this many rows first (paging: next offset = offset + count).

params.name: --coarse
params.help: Group by coarse signature (level + logger + masked message; no exceptions).

params.name: --columns
params.help: Columns to return: comma-separated (signature,count) and/or repeated.

params.name: --brief
params.help: Only signature, template, level_name, logger, exception_type, count, first_seen, last_seen.

show.description:
Show the entries of one group, with the variables extracted from each message.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "entries.v1", "logset": id, "signature": str,
   "group": {<groups.v1 row>} | null, "count": int,
   "items": [{<entries.v1 row: id, ts, level, level_name, thread, logger,
              message, body, user, ..., exception_type, signature,
              template, variables, source_path, source_line, raw, ...>}, ...]}
"variables" lists the values that masking replaced in the template, in
order (issue keys, numbers, ids ...). Entries are ordered by time.
SIGNATURE may be a unique prefix of at least 4 hex characters (resolved
via the groups table; "signature" echoes the full one); a prefix that
matches several groups is error "ambiguous" listing up to 5 "candidates".
"raw" and "body" are cut to --max-raw characters (default 4000 in json/jsonl,
no limit in table and --raw mode); a cut text ends with
"… [truncated: N chars total, use --max-raw 0]" and its row gets
"body_truncated": true and "raw_chars": <original length of raw> (both keys
only on cut rows).
With --raw the original log text of each entry is printed instead (any
--output mode), entries separated by a blank line (or, when colour is on,
highlighted and separated by a source:line rule).
--columns keeps only the named entry columns (as `entries --columns`).
--brief is the preset --columns id,ts,level_name,thread,user,request_id,
logger,message,exception_type,signature,variables and also cuts "group"
to signature,template,level_name,logger,exception_type,count,first_seen,
last_seen; --brief with --columns is a usage error.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad option, unknown column, --brief with --columns, or
ambiguous signature prefix; 2 no entries with this signature; 3 unknown set
or store error.

params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name.

params.name: SIGNATURE
params.help: Group signature (from `groups`) or a unique prefix of it (4+ hex chars).

params.name: --limit
params.help: Maximum number of entries; 0 = all.

params.name: --raw
params.help: Print the raw log text of the entries (highlighted when colour is on).

params.name: --max-raw
params.help: Characters kept of raw and body per entry; 0 = no limit. Default: 4000 in json/jsonl mode, no limit in table and --raw mode.

params.name: --columns
params.help: Entry columns to return: comma-separated (ts,message) and/or repeated.

params.name: --brief
params.help: Only id, ts, level_name, thread, user, request_id, logger, message, exception_type, signature, variables; "group" in its --brief form.

entries.usage: LOGSET [--signature str] [--coarse-signature str] [--level str] [--min-level str] [--logger str] [--user str] [--thread str] [--request-id str] [--since str] [--until str] [--contains str] [--with-exception] [--exception str] [--node str] [--columns str*] [--brief] [--limit int=100] [--offset int=0] [--raw] [--max-raw int] [--window overlap|union]
entries.description:
List entries of a log set (or of all nodes of a capture), filtered, ordered by time.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "entries.v1", "logset": id, "count": int, "total": int,
   "offset": int, "next_offset": int | null, "truncated": bool,
   "items": [<entries.v1 row>, ...]}
"total" counts the matching entries before --offset/--limit; "offset"
echoes --offset; "truncated" is true when more entries follow this page
and "next_offset" is where it starts (offset + count; null on the last
page). --coarse-signature takes the signature of `groups --coarse`. With
--raw the raw log text of the entries is printed instead (as `show --raw`;
--offset/--limit apply).
Rows hold all entries.v1 columns (`ragnalog schema entries`; ts is UTC,
level numeric) unless --columns is given:
  id, ts, tz_offset, level, level_name, thread, logger, message, body, user,
  request_id, session, ip, url, request_url, context, exception_type,
  exception_message, exception_chain, signature, coarse_signature, template,
  variables, source_path, source_line, source_offset, raw, parse_error
--columns takes comma-separated names and/or is repeated
(--columns ts,level_name --columns message); an unknown name is error
"invalid_value" whose "hint" lists the valid columns. --brief is the
preset --columns id,ts,level_name,thread,user,request_id,logger,message,
exception_type,signature; --brief with --columns is a usage error.
--with-exception keeps entries with an exception (exception_type not
null) at any level; --exception TEXT matches a case-insensitive substring
of exception_type (the outermost exception).
"raw" and "body" are cut to --max-raw characters (default 4000 in
json/jsonl, no limit in table and --raw mode); a cut text ends with
"… [truncated: N chars total, use --max-raw 0]" and its row gets
"body_truncated": true and "raw_chars": <original length of raw> (of body
when raw is not among --columns); both keys appear only on cut rows.
A capture (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@YYYY-MM-DD]) gives the entries of all
its nodes interleaved by time (then node): "logset" is capture:ID and each
row adds "node" and "set" (the node's set id). They are taken from the
capture's window: --since/--until, else --window (overlap, the time all
nodes have logs for, by default; union); --signature is resolved in any
node's groups and may name several, comma-separated (entries of any of
them), each also NODE:SIGNATURE (that group on that node only: both
sides of a co-burst); --node N1,N2 keeps the entries of those nodes (the window stays
that of all nodes); --columns may name node and set. With --raw and
colour on, each entry's rule names its node.

Exit codes: 0 ok (also when nothing matches); 1 bad option, unknown
column, --brief with --columns, --window, --node, several signatures or
NODE:SIGNATURE with a set, a node not in the capture, or ambiguous
--signature prefix;
2 unknown capture or no such group in the capture; 3 unknown set or
store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name; or a capture (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@YYYY-MM-DD]).

params.name: --signature

context.description:

--before entries preceding ENTRY_ID and the --after entries following it
in time order (ties in file order), restricted to the anchor's thread

   "items": [<entries.v1 row>, ...]}

"raw" and "body" are cut as in `entries` (--max-raw, default 4000 in
json/jsonl). In jsonl mode one row per line; the anchor row has an extra

is the preset --columns id,ts,level_name,thread,user,request_id,logger,
message,exception_type,signature,variables; --brief with --columns is a
usage error.

of all nodes of the set's capture within --window seconds before and
after the anchor (all threads; --before/--after/--any-thread do not
apply), in time then node order, at most 2000 (the nearest; "truncated"
and "total" say so); rows add "node" and "set", "any_thread" is true.

first --limit application frames: frames whose class is outside the
library packages (JDK, Groovy, Jira platform: com.atlassian., org.ofbiz.,
webwork., org.apache., com.google., JDBC drivers, ...), so plugin code
stands out. With the environment variable RAGNALOG_APP_PACKAGES set
(comma-separated prefixes, e.g. com.acme.,org.example.) an application
frame is one that starts with one of those prefixes instead.

parsed exception). "app_frames" holds at most --limit frames and

frames printed in the log, "omitted_frames" the "... N more" count.
"frames" (every frame with an "app" flag) and all application frames are
returned only with --all.

per line; the table prints each exception and its frames as text.

query.description:
Run DuckDB SQL over a log set and print the result rows.

Views: "entries" (entries.v1), "groups" (groups.v1) and "merges" (merges.v1,
only when present). Their columns (types and descriptions: `ragnalog
schema entries|groups|merges`):
  entries:
    id, ts, tz_offset, level, level_name, thread, logger, message, body, user,
    request_id, session, ip, url, request_url, context, exception_type,
    exception_message, exception_chain, signature, coarse_signature, template,
    variables, source_path, source_line, source_offset, raw, parse_error
  groups:
    signature, coarse_signature, template, level, level_name, logger,
    exception_type, count, first_seen, last_seen, user_count, thread_count,
    source_count, top_users, top_threads, sources, examples
  merges:
    cluster_id, drain_template, signatures
level is numeric (TRACE=10 DEBUG=20 INFO=30 WARN=40 ERROR=50 FATAL=60),
ts/first_seen/last_seen are UTC timestamps, variables a list of strings.
The session time zone is UTC whatever the machine's zone: result
timestamps are UTC (as in `entries`) and date_trunc('day', ts) buckets
at UTC midnight. One statement only (several are a usage error).

SQL examples:
  select level, count(*) n from entries group by 1 order by 2 desc
  select unnest(variables) v, count(*) n from entries
    where signature = '0123456789abcdef' group by 1 order by 2 desc
  select signature, count, template from groups where exception_type is not null
    order by count desc limit 20

Output (json):
  {"schema": "query.v1", "logset": id, "columns": [str, ...], "count": int,
   "total": int, "truncated": false, "items": [{<column>: value, ...}, ...]}
The CLI never truncates query results ("total" = "count"); use LIMIT in SQL.

Errors: "sql_error"; for an unknown column its "hint" lists DuckDB's
candidate columns (or the columns of the views), for an unknown table the
available views.

Exit codes: 0 ok (also for an empty result); 1 SQL error; 3 unknown set or
store error.

Count entries per time bucket: of a log set, or per node of a capture.

A log set gives timeline.v1 (as GET /api/sets/{ref}/timeline). A capture
reference (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@DAY]), or a set with --by-node, gives

last bucket index in which the node has logs; with --signature "levels"
has only "count". A set with --by-level adds "levels" to each bucket:

(unknown level): n}. Table mode prints one row per bucket (a capture: one
column per node; --by-level: one column per level).

a set, --node with a set, --by-level with a capture, several signatures of

Compare the groups of two log sets (A = before, B = after).

"new": signatures present only in B; "vanished": only in A; "changed": in
both with a different count (ratio = count_b / count_a). Only the stored
group tables are compared, never the raw logs.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "diff.v1", "a": id_a, "b": id_b,
   "new": [row], "vanished": [row], "changed": [row], "unchanged_count": int,
   "totals": {"new": int, "vanished": int, "changed": int}, "truncated": bool,
   "warnings": [str]}
Each section holds at most --limit rows (default 50, 0 = all); "totals"
are the section sizes before --limit and "truncated" is true when any
section was cut.
Each row has signature, template, level, level_name, logger,
exception_type, count_a, count_b, first_seen_a, last_seen_a, first_seen_b,
last_seen_b (counts are 0 on the missing side); "changed" rows also have
ratio. "new" is sorted by count_b, "vanished" by count_a, "changed" by
|log(ratio)|, all descending. With --rate "changed" rows also have rate_a
and rate_b (count per hour of each set's span, first to last entry) and
rate_ratio = rate_b / rate_a, and "changed" is sorted by rate_ratio
descending: use it when the sets cover different lengths of time.
"warnings" is present only when the spans of A and B differ by more than
4x either way: one sentence saying that new/vanished groups are
unreliable (groups that occur only at certain times of day). In table and
jsonl mode the sentence goes to stderr. In jsonl mode one row per line
with an extra "change" key (new / vanished / changed).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 the sets were built with different signature/mask-rule
versions or specs (use --force); 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: SET_A
params.help: Baseline log set (id, id prefix or name).

params.name: SET_B
params.help: Log set to compare against the baseline.

params.name: --min-level
params.help: Only groups of this level or more severe (e.g. ERROR).

params.name: --level
params.help: Alias of --min-level: this level and above (unlike `entries --level`, which matches exactly).

params.name: --coarse
params.help: Compare by coarse signature (exception chain ignored).

params.name: --force
params.help: Compare even if signature versions or specs differ.

params.name: --limit
params.help: Maximum rows per section (new, vanished, changed); 0 = all.

params.name: --rate
params.help: Add hourly rates (rate_a, rate_b, rate_ratio) to "changed" and sort it by rate_ratio, for sets of different length.

triage.description:
Answer "are there new kinds of errors since the baseline?" in one document.

Compares SET with a baseline (as `diff BASELINE SET --min-level L`) and
sorts the result for a decision: new groups (most severe first), new
groups of a lower level that carry an exception, groups whose hourly rate
grew, vanished groups. --baseline auto (default) ranks the other sets of
the same format (the web app's rule): it rejects a set signed with
another recipe_key (reason "stale", hint `upgrade`; or "recipe"), whose
sources are a superset or subset of SET's ("superset"/"subset"; partial
overlap is fine), that ends after SET ("later"), that has under 1% of
SET's entries ("tiny") or a span more than 16x longer or shorter
("span"); of the rest it prefers a set that ends before SET starts, then
the span closest to SET's, then the newest. With none left the verdict
is no_baseline and "warnings" lists the rejected sets. An explicit
--baseline is used as given, with a warning when it is stale, contained
or tiny.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "triage.v1",
   "set": {"id", "name", "first_ts", "last_ts", "entries"},
   "baseline": {"id", "name", "first_ts", "last_ts",
                "resolved_by": "auto" | "param", "reason": str,
                "entries": int, "shared_sources": int,
                "candidates": [{"id", "name", "reason", "detail",
                                "hint"?}, ...]} | null,
   "min_level": "WARN",
   "verdict": "new_errors" | "new_warnings" | "new_exceptions" | "clean"
              | "no_baseline",
   "summary": {"new", "new_by_level": {"ERROR": n, ...}, "new_exceptions",
               "grew", "vanished", "changed", "unchanged"} | null,
   "coverage": {"hours_baseline", "hours_set", "ratio"},
   "warnings": [str, ...],
   "new": [<diff row> + "rate_per_hour"],
   "new_exceptions": [<diff row> + "rate_per_hour"],
   "grew": [<diff row> + "ratio", "rate_a", "rate_b", "rate_ratio"],
   "vanished": [<diff row>]}
Diff rows are those of `diff` (signature, template, level, level_name,
logger, exception_type, count_a, count_b, first/last_seen_a/b); set and
baseline timestamps are written as in their manifests.
"new": groups at/above --min-level only in SET; "new_exceptions": new
groups of ANY level with an exception that are not in "new" (a new DEBUG
stack trace); "grew": changed groups whose hourly rate rose at least --grow
times (rates as `diff --rate`, which normalise different spans), highest
rate_ratio first; "vanished": groups at
/above --min-level only in the baseline. "verdict": new_errors (a new
ERROR/FATAL group), new_warnings (other new groups), new_exceptions (no
new group but a new exception at a lower level), clean, no_baseline.
"coverage" gives both spans in hours and ratio = hours_set /
hours_baseline; when they differ by more than 4x either way "warnings"
says that "new"/"vanished" are unreliable (a nightly set lacks daytime
groups). "baseline.reason" says why the baseline was chosen,
"shared_sources" counts the source files both sets share and
"candidates" lists up to 5 rejected sets (auto only). Lists hold at most
--limit rows; "summary" counts all.
jsonl mode prints the document on one line. Table mode prints the
verdict, the summary and one table per list; the warnings go to stderr.

SET is one set: a capture reference is a usage error, as `capture REF
--triage` gives the verdict of each node against its own previous set.

Exit codes: 0 ok, whatever the verdict (also no_baseline); 1 bad option,
invalid level, a capture reference, or the sets were built with different
signature/mask-rule versions or specs; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: The log set to judge (id, id prefix or name).

params.name: --baseline
params.help: Baseline set (id, id prefix or name), auto, or none (verdict no_baseline).

params.name: --min-level
params.help: Only groups of this level or more severe count as new/grew/vanished.

params.name: --grow
params.help: Minimum hourly-rate factor for "grew" (> 1).

params.name: --limit
params.help: Maximum rows per list; 0 = all.

report.usage: LOGSET [--out path] [--compare str] [--min-level str] [--examples int=3] [--max-raw int=4000] [--max-groups int] [--window overlap|union] [--open]
report.description:
Write a self-contained HTML report of a set or capture (the cluster page).

The page needs no network access (CSS, JS and data are inlined) and works
from a file share or an e-mail attachment: overview tiles, a per-hour
timeline by level (drag to select a time window), the filterable group
table and a detail drawer per group with example entries and the
equivalent CLI commands. The embedded data is the "report.v1" payload
(docs/formats/report.v1.md). With --compare SET_B the report shows the
groups of SET relative to SET_B (SET_B = baseline, as `diff SET_B SET`).
A capture (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@YYYY-MM-DD]) gives the cluster page
(the "cluster-report.v1" payload, docs/cluster.md): node cards with each
node's triage verdict, a timeline band per node with its events, the
groups by node, interactions and the example entries of all nodes, within
--window (overlap by default, or union). The default file is
<cluster>_<capture id>.html; --compare and --min-level apply to sets only.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "report-file.v1", "path": str, "bytes": int, "groups": int,
   "entries": int, "compare": bool, "capture"?: str | null, "nodes"?: int}
"groups" is the number of groups in the report, "entries" the number of
embedded example entries; a capture adds "capture" (its id) and "nodes".
Table mode prints one line.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad option, invalid level, --out is a directory, or the
sets were built with different signature/mask-rule versions or specs; 2 the
output directory does not exist or unknown capture; 3 unknown set or store
error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name; or a capture (capture:ID, cluster:NAME[@YYYY-MM-DD]).

params.name: --out
params.help: Output file; default <name or id>.html in the current directory.

params.name: --compare
params.help: Baseline log set to compare with (id, id prefix or name).

params.name: --min-level
params.help: Only groups of this level or more severe (e.g. WARN); the overview always covers the whole set.

params.name: --examples
params.help: Example entries per group (a capture: per group and node); 0 = none.

params.name: --max-raw
params.help: Truncate each example's raw text to this many characters; 0 = no limit.

params.name: --max-groups
params.help: Only the N largest groups; 0 = all. Default: all (a capture: 500).

params.name: --window
params.help: overlap or union (a capture only; default overlap).

params.name: --open
params.help: Open the report in the default web browser.

parse.description:
Parse log files and stream the entries as JSON Lines to stdout (no data directory).

Always writes JSONL, one entry per line, regardless of --output:
  {"id", "format", "timestamp" (ISO 8601 with offset), "level" (name),
   "thread", "logger", "message", "body", "exception_type",
   "exceptions": [{"type", "message", "frames": [{"location", "file",
                   "line", "module"}], "omitted_frames"}],
   "context": {"user", "request_id", "session", "ip", "url", "request_url", ...},
   "source": {"path", "line", "offset"}, "raw", "parse_error"}
Entries whose header could not be parsed have "parse_error" set. Files
found in a directory that are not in the format are skipped, and a large
named file not in the format is refused (as `ingest`).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 unknown --format; 2 no files, format not detected, a
large named file not in the format, or no entries.

params.name: PATHS...
params.help: Log files and/or directories.

params.name: --format
params.help: Format name; detected from the first 200 lines when omitted.

params.name: --limit
params.help: Stop after this many entries; 0 = all.

params.name: --force
params.help: Read a named file over 64 MiB even if it is not in the format.

regroup.description:
Recompute the groups of a stored log set with another signature spec.

Re-signs the stored entries (each distinct level, logger, message and
exception chain once) and rewrites the signature columns of
entries.parquet and groups.parquet; every other column is kept.
Signatures change, so diffs against sets built with another spec need
--force. Prints the updated manifest (new signature_spec and recipe_key).

Output (json): the manifest, {"schema": "logset.v1", ...} (see `ingest`).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 bad option; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name.

params.name: --frames
params.help: Include the top N stack frames of each exception in the signature.

params.name: --no-exceptions
params.help: Leave the exception chain out of the signature (like --coarse).

upgrade.description:
Rebuild stale log sets at the current recipe, each with its own spec.

A set is stale ("stale": true in `sets`) when its recipe_key (format
version, signature spec, signature and masking-rule versions) differs from
the recipe this version signs its format and spec with; stale sets are not
comparable with new ones, and triage skips them as baselines. upgrade
re-signs the stored entries as `regroup` does, keeping each set's
signature spec. A set built by an older version of its format is also
re-assembled from its stored entries (Jira sets of format version 1:
banner lines join the entry they announce); the log files are not read.
Sets that are current, or whose format is not registered, are skipped
with a reason. A set ingested from a ZIP by an older version names its
files by the spool directory they were extracted to (removed since):
upgrade renames them to <zip>/<member>, stale or not.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "upgrade.v1", "count": int, "upgraded": int,
   "items": [<logset.v1 manifest without "schema"> +
             {"status": "upgraded" | "skipped", "reason": str | null,
              "previous_recipe_key": str, "renamed_sources"?: int}, ...]}
"reason" is null for an upgraded set, "current" for a set already at the
current recipe, or names the unknown format or spec. Items follow the
order of SET arguments (with --all: the `sets` order, newest first).

Exit codes: 0 ok (also when everything was skipped); 1 no SET and no
--all; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSETS...
params.help: Log sets to upgrade (id, unique id prefix or name).

params.name: --all
params.help: Upgrade every set in the data directory.

formats.description:
List the supported log formats.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "formats.v1", "count": int,
   "items": [{"name", "description", "signature_spec", "mask_rules": [str]}]}
With --sample FILE each item also has "confidence" (0..1) from sniffing the
first 200 lines of FILE, and items are sorted by it.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 --sample is a directory; 2 sample file not found.

params.name: --sample
params.help: A log file to test every format against.

schema.description:
Print the JSON description of a stored table or the JSON Schema of a document.

"entries", "groups" and "merges" are the Parquet tables (also the views
available to `query`); "logset" is manifest.json. A document name such
as "triage.v1" prints the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of that document,
as in docs/formats/<name>.schema.json; rows are described by the tables'
columns, all optional. Without NAME the four tables are printed and
"documents" lists the document names.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "schema.v1", "definitions": {<name>: <schema description>, ...},
   "documents": [str, ...]}
"documents" only without NAME. In table mode the same document is
pretty-printed as JSON.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 unknown NAME.

params.name: NAME
params.help: A table (entries, groups, merges, logset) or a document, e.g. triage.v1.

manifest.description:
Print how an agent uses ragnalog: workflow, commands and documents (about 10 KB).

The workflow in order with a one-line purpose per step, when to use the
other commands, every command (usage with types and defaults, output
document, exit codes), one-line help per parameter, the documents
(`ragnalog schema NAME`), the --brief presets, the environment variables
and the global options. Bare `ragnalog` prints the same document when
stdout is not a terminal; GET /api/manifest of the web app too.
`manifest COMMAND` prints one command in full instead: its --help text and
every parameter with type, default and help (GET /api/manifest/COMMAND).

Output (json):
  {"schema": "manifest.v1", "tool", "version", "usage", "notes",
   "workflow": [{"run", "purpose"}], "when": [{"run", "purpose"}],
   "commands": {<name>: {"summary", "usage", "output", "exit": [int]}},
   "help": {<parameter>: str}, "global_options", "exit_codes",
   "documents": {"get", "names"}, "presets", "env"}
  {"schema": "manifest-command.v1", "command", "version", "usage",
   "description", "output", "exit": [int],
   "params": [{"name", "type", "default", "help"}]}
In table mode the same document is pretty-printed as JSON.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 unknown COMMAND.

params.name: COMMAND
params.help: One command to describe in full (default: the whole manifest).

remove.description:
Delete a log set from the data directory (its directory and all files).

Output (json): {"schema": "remove.v1", "removed": id, "name": str | null}

A set whose manifest.json cannot be read is removed by its directory name
("name" is then null).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 3 unknown set or store error.

params.name: LOGSET
params.help: Log set id, unique id prefix or name (the directory name when the manifest cannot be read).

serve.description:
Run the web app over the store: browse, compare and triage sets, upload new logs.

Pages: / (sets with triage verdicts and upload), /sets/SET (interactive
report, ?compare=auto|SET), /sets/SET/triage. JSON API under /api with
the same documents as this CLI (OpenAPI at /docs). Needs the `web` extra.

Output: server log on stderr until interrupted (Ctrl+C); nothing on stdout
("schema": none).

Exit codes: 0 stopped normally; 1 the `web` extra is not installed or bad
option; 3 store error (including the default ./.ragnalog not existing inside
a git work tree: pass --store DIR or set RAGNALOG_STORE, and another server
already using the data directory: one server per data directory).

params.name: --host
params.help: Interface to bind; use 0.0.0.0 to serve the network (set --token then).

params.name: --port
params.help: TCP port.

params.name: --token
params.help: Require `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` on /api (env RAGNALOG_TOKEN).

params.name: --max-upload-mb
params.help: Largest accepted upload in MiB (env RAGNALOG_MAX_UPLOAD_MB; default 2048).

params.name: --allowed-host
params.help: Comma-separated host names a loopback server also answers, e.g. the public name behind a reverse proxy that passes Host through (env RAGNALOG_ALLOWED_HOSTS; on loopback every other name is refused).

params.name: --reload
params.help: Restart on code changes (development); the settings above reach the reloading process through the RAGNALOG_* environment variables.

version.description:
Print tool, schema and signature versions.

Output (json):
  {"schema": "version.v1", "version": str, "schema_version": str,
   "signature_version": int, "mask_rules_version": int, "python": str}

Exit codes: 0 ok.

batch.description:
Run many commands in one process: argv arrays in, one JSON document per line out.

Reads JSON Lines from stdin, one command per line as a JSON array of its
arguments without "ragnalog" and without global options, e.g.
  ["groups", "prod", "--brief", "--limit", "5"]
  ["show", "prod", "0a1b2c3d"]
Each runs in this process with the global --store (and the other global
options) and --output json, and writes exactly one JSON document per line
to stdout, in input order: its usual document, or error.v1 when it fails
(a line that is not a JSON array of strings, a global option, --help, or
batch/parse/serve, which do not write one document, are usage errors).
Every error message starts with "line N:".
Blank lines are skipped. A failed line never stops the batch.
Use it to avoid the start-up cost of the CLI (about 0.45 s per call) when
an agent runs several commands.

Output: one document per input line, each with its own "schema"
("groups.v1", "entries.v1", ..., "error.v1"); diagnostics on stderr.

Exit codes: 0 when the input was read, whatever each line returned; 1 the
input could not be read (not UTF-8, or a read error).
